description.narrative: Insatsen var initialt ett stöd till FN:s nya landprogram för Kenya, Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (SDCF), 2022-2026, som kanaliseras genom en Multi Partner Trust Fund för ändamålet. Det svenska stödet ska främst användas för kapacitetsstärkning av MPTF:s management i Nairobi, inklusive sekretariatet för SDG Partnership Platform, båda inhysta under UN Resident Coordinator's Office (UNRCO). Kapacitetsstärkningen riktar sig främst mot områdena ungdomar och sysselsättning; katastrofriskreduceringe och resiliens; miljö, klimat och grön finansiering samt hanteringen av SDGPP. Ytterligare bidrag har därefter givits till fonden för att stödja särskilda ändamål genom sk Joint Programs.

The contribution was initially a support to the UN:s new country program for Kenya - the Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (SDCF), 2022-2026, which is channeled through the Multi Partner Trust Fund set up for this purpose. The Swedish support will primarily be used for capacity strengthening of the MPTF's management in Nairobi, including the Secretariat for the SDG Partnership Platform, both hosted within the UN Resident Coordinator's Office (UNRCO). The capacity strengthening is focused on the areas of youth and employment; disaster risk reduction and resilience; environment, climate and green financing; and SDGPP management. Additional contributions to the Fund have thereafter been provided for special purposes through so called Joint Programs.

The main objectives of the intervention are:
- improved coordination of the UNCT, together with GoK, donors and other stakeholders, for a more effective and efficient implementation of the UNSDCF in alignment with Kenya's development plans;
- contribute to enhanced resource mobilization through the SDGPP and development of innovative finance solutions for investments in prioritised sectors (and sub-sectors) as identfied by Kenya and in the SDCF.
The SDG MPTF Kenya was established in July 2022, with the purpose to support the delivery of UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2022 2026, enhance the UN to deliver as one through Joint Programs and to support the country in achieving the SDGs. The Fund builds on the existing Partnerships Platform (SDGPP) that was established in 2017 to support the UNDAF 20182022. Sida's first contribution is loosely earmarked to the Fund's "Enabler Window", and more specifically for Strengthening the Capacity of the SDG MPTF Kenya Secretariat (the Secretariat) by financing four positions at the RCO and SDGPP, as well as a smaller budget for "emerging, strategic issues". A second contribution to the Fund was agreed upon in a first amendment to the MPTF SAA and disbursed in late December 2022, earmarked for a Joint Program on drought response and resilience under the Window for Strategic Pillar 2, "Planet and Prosperity". A third contribution to the Fund was agreed upon in a second amendment to the MPTF SAA and disbursed in late December 2023, earmarked for a bridge Joint Program on Social and Child Protection under the Window for Strategic Pillar 1, "People and Peace". The objectives of the intervention have, thus, been updated with regards to the additional funding to the MPTF by these amendments.
The main objectives of the intervention are: - improved coordination of the UNCT, together with GoK, donors and other stakeholders, for a more effective and efficient implementation of the UNSDCF in alignment with Kenya's development plans; - contribute to enhanced resource mobilization through the SDGPP and development of innovative finance solutions for investments in prioritized sectors (and sub-sectors) as identified by Kenya and in the SDCF.
For amendment I: The main purpose and overall objective is to enhance response and recovery for communities affected by drought in Northern Kenya while enhancing long term climate resilience response and recovery targeting 75,000 people and 200,000 livestock. The specific objectives are: - to provide improved access to safe water and hygiene for 75,000 drought affected vulnerable people and 200,000 livestock in Turkana, Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, and Marsabit counties by ensuring continued availability and access to essential services and strengthened climate smart food production for 1,000 households impacted by the drought in Garissa, Turkana and Tana River counties.
For amendment II: The expected results are: - To enhance the capacity and opportunities for the poor and vulnerable to improve and sustain their livelihoods and welfare; - To facilitate and follow up successful achievement of government's commitment to expand social protection coverage including cost sharing whenever possible; - Social and child protection systems have enhanced technical and financial capacity to develop and manage programs at scale; - Functional coordination at the national and county levels for inter-sectoral linkages is enhanced; - Government and partners have financial and technical capacity to review, develop and implement policies, legislation and strategies delivering on the right to social protection and child protection-
For amendment III: The expected results for the Joint Program are: - To support coordination, data management and evidence based policymaking, planning and budgeting for enhanced child protection and social protection outcomes - Enhanced systems and capacity of the national and county governments, non-state institutions and communities to efficiently deliver well-coordinated, inclusive, accessible, equitable and resilient/shock-responsive social and child protection services to Kenyans, addressing multiple dimensions of poverty and vulnerability across the life cycle. -Enhanced capacity of national and county governments, non state institutions and communities to strengthen and expand inclusive and sustainable child protection and social protection programmes and systems For this Joint Program Swedish contribution to the MPTF, the interventions objectives are hereby updated with regards to the funding for Social and Child Protection

description.narrative:
The Fund Reports annually in May on Fund Status and Progress as per the previous calendar year. The Annual Report submitted in May 2025, hence, covers the period 1st January to 31st December 2024 and provides a detailed summary of consolidated results and achievements as well as the financial status of the MPTF.
During 2024, Sweden's contributions to the MPTF has continued to support the RCO through the Enabler Window, and also funded Joint Programs for Social and Child Protection (a bridging program as well as an additional contribution to a new long-term JP).
Examples of results and achievements reported include:
Under the Enabler Window, the Secretariat:
- continues to strategically drive the shift from fragmented projects within the UN Country Team (UNCT) to unified, multi-sectoral programming, promoting catalytic use of resources for policy leverage and co-financing. As of December 2024, a total of 17 Participating UN Agencies (PUNOs) had signed up as members of the Fund.
- provided targeted technical support to the State Department for Labour and Skills Development in developing institutional frameworks and policy guidance for employment and skills. A key outcome was the draft National Strategy on Green Skills and Jobs, aiming to advance a green economy that enhances human well-being and social equity while reducing environmental risks.
- faiclitated engagement with Cabinet Secretaries, particularly the Ministry of Youth Affairs, Creative Economy and Sports, presenting emerging initiatives, including digital participatory platforms such as zKe: Youth Voices; and achieved a mutual commitment to jointly fast-track critical youth priorities, including the National Youth Council Elections and the Youth Bill 2024.
- provided technical advisory and coordination support to the Joint Sector Working Group on Climate, Environment & Forestry (JSWG), a high-level platform that facilitates dialogue between development partners and the Government of Kenya, to align on updated national priorities including the development of carbon markets, follow-up actions from the Africa Climate Summit and the review of Kenyas Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0).
- played a catalytic role in advancing a coordinated, system-wide approach to Disaster Risk Management (DRM) at both national and sub-national levels. Through technical support, policy guidance and multi-stakeholder facilitation, the Secretariat ensured joint action on DRM legislation, harmonised humanitarian response mechanisms and integrated planning across agencies, which was particularly instrumental in response to two major flooding episodes during the year. These efforts to mobilise coordinated technical and financial support resulted in immediate humanitarian assistance and a unified response reaching 190,000 individuals across 10 counties during the March to May season and 281,835 people during the October to December season.
- Moreover, the Secretariat's Fund for emerging opportunities (as part of Sweden's contribution) were used for the following initiatives:
* the Futures Summit, in collaboration with the UN Futures Lab * the Food Systems Summit (FSS); * the Peacebuilding Architecture Review; * the National Tree Planting Programme; and * the zKe Initiative, aimed at empowering youth and enhancing their sustained engagement in Kenyas democratic and governance processes.
Under the People and Peace Thematic Window
* Sweden contributed with one year's funding to the bridging JP for Social and Child Protection (implemented by WFP and UNICEF). Selected results from this intervention include:
- transformative results through support to GoK to significantly scale up the Inua Jamii social cash transfer programme, increasing coverage from 1.028 million to 1.703 million households, the first major expansion in over a decade.
- enhancement of the Management Information System (MIS) and development of data collection tools and training for enumerators. Notably, eligibility criteria for the Cash Transfer for Orphans and Vulnerable Children (CT-OVC) were revised to better capture child protection vulnerabilities, contributing to more inclusive programming.
- facilitation of the integration of the Enhanced Single Registry with the National Health Insurance Fund, enabling social protection beneficiaries to access universal health services in multiple counties, laying the groundwork for long-term systems strengthening and service integration.
- six regulations and four Rules of Court were finalised under the Children Act 2022
- finalisation and Cabinet approval of the Kenya Social Protection Policy 2023, which adopts a lifecycle approach (i.e. addressing multiple dimensions of poverty and vulnerability across the life cycle)
- the development of disability-inclusive regulations that promote employment, access to services and business-friendly provisions.
- finalisation and Cabinet submission of the National Policy for Persons with Disabilities, which strengthens Kenyas policy coherence and commitment to inclusion.
- Collectively, these efforts reflect the JPs strategic contribution to systems strengthening, legal accountability and long-term sustainability of inclusive social protection across national and sub-national levels.
- the JP made significant strides in integrating gender, disability and child protection into Kenyas broader social protection architecture. A landmark gender analysis commissioned by UN Kenya is now guiding national reforms, while UN Kenya also supported the development of a National Action Plan for Persons with Disabilities and Caregivers to inform inclusive programme design.
- the Wajir County Disability Fund expanded its reach to 830 beneficiaries, providing monthly stipends, assistive devices and income-generating support. This disability-inclusive initiative was showcased at the 17th UN Conference of States Parties to the CRPD.
- a gender-responsive care system was co-designed with the government, to address the burden of unpaid care, especially on women, offering a scalable model for care reform.
- scale-up of Kenyas Care Reform Programme, now active in 16 counties. In Nairobis Kasarani sub-county alone, 234 children were reunified with families, 18 placed in foster care and 33 supported through independent living.
Nevertheless, despite the landmark expansion of Inua Jamii, poor children still remain substantially under-covered. The Cash Transfer for Orphans and Vulnerable Children reaches just 11% of the number of children in multidimensional poverty.
* During 2024, Sweden also contributed with additional funding for two years to the new JP for Social and Child Protection, launched in June 2024 and to be implemented by WFP, UNICEF, ILO and FAO. Since the disbursement to the MPTF only was made in October 2024, and in December to the PUNOs, no activities were carried out during this reporting period and results can, hence, not be attributed to this reporting period.
* Financially, an additional amount of 12.3 MUSD was contributed to the MPTF during 2024, of which Sweden disbursed nearly 8 MUSD. The MPTF is currently being financed by 10 contributors, with a total amount thus committed amounting to about 30 MUSD, of which Sweden has committed about 19 MUSD. Out of the total committed amount, 13.5 MUSD had been deposited in the Fund by 31 December 2024, of which the Fund had transferred a cumulative net amount of 16.4 MUSD to 13 PUNOs, hence leaving a Fund balance of 33%. In turn, the cumulative expenditures reported by the PUNOs, amounted to 8.9 MUSD by 31 December 2024, which equates to an overall Fund expenditure delivery rate of 54.5 percent. This raises some concerns about effectiveness
Sweden is still the largest donor to the Fund, accounting for 63% of the commitments and 55% of all deposits, followed by Norway (20%). This raises concerns about dependency of very few donors/sources of income.
The Fund's balance by end 2024 was 33% and its expenditure rate 54.5%. This raises concerns about effectiveness but can partly be explained by the slow creation and endorsement by Government of Kenya on the planned Joint Programs to be financed through the Fund. In addition, the balance is also due to some donors depositing their contributions as a one-off instalment but to be utilised over several years.
